full_dataset_size: 1 file, booking-listings.csv, 62,784,719 bytes (~63 MB); HF size tag 10K<n<100K rows; extrapolating 5,896 rows per 4.9 MB gives roughly 75k rows
description: Booking.com search-result listings captured by Bright Data (a commercial scraper vendor) and published on HuggingFace: one row per property returned for a search (city/region, check-in date, adults, rooms) with quoted final_price vs original_price in USD, free-cancellation and no-prepayment flags, cancellation deadline, bedroom/bed/kitchen counts, review score and count, and sustainability JSON. Grain is listing x search; check-ins are six dates from 27 Dec 2024 to 27 Feb 2025, so it is a one-off cross-section, not a time series; the head spans 50 country codes (India, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, US, Vietnam, Thailand, Italy lead). For ABNB an analyst would use it as a competitor-pricing and payment-terms backdrop: the share of Booking.com inventory offered with no prepayment (39% in the head; free_cancellation is 100% in the head, so the capture was probably filtered on that flag) and the discount depth (29% of rows discounted, median 22%) frame the RNPL / cancellation thesis, and nb_bedrooms > 0 (31% of rows) isolates alternative-accommodation units for a capacity/party-size comparison against Inside Airbnb.
issues: Licence is 'other' = Bright Data Master Service Agreement, not an open licence; the CSV is world-readable without a token but redistribution rights are unclear, so only a 5 MB head was taken and the remaining ~58 MB was NOT fetched pending a human licence decision (tos_or_license_flag=true). Data provenance is a scraper vendor's marketing sample, one-off cross-section with a 100% free_cancellation share (likely a filtered search), so cancellation shares are not representative of all Booking.com inventory. Eight columns (country, hotel_rank, searched_country, map_coordinates, listing_country, total_listings_found, star_rating, tags) are entirely null in the head; listing country was recovered from the /hotel/<cc>/ path in url instead. One row priced in BRL, the rest USD. No scraper was run; no airbnb.com contact.
